title: Positive fibre degrees give a projective-bundle embedding
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes (each has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), and suppose each geometric fibre has dimension at most $1$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every geometric point $x\to X$ and each one-dimensional irreducible component $Z$ of the reduced fibre $Y_x$, the degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] of $\mathcal L$ pulled back to the normalization of $Z$ is positive. Then $\mathcal L$ is $f$-ample: over each affine open $U\subset X$ its restriction is an ample invertible module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is a positive integer $n$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ with a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_X(\mathcal E)$ pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$. Thus $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre], and dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Normalization of an integral component has the meaning of [def-sc-normalization].

source.place: Stacks Tags 0B5Y, varieties.tex, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components (normalization degree is unchanged by finite birational pullback); 0D2S, more-morphisms.tex, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood; 01VU, morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample and lemma-relatively-very-ample. Proper coherent pushforward makes f_*L^n finite type; properness makes its immersion closed.

proof.text: Because $f$ is proper, it is of finite type by the definition of properness. The geometric fibre over $x\to X$ is the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(x)}\to X$. Properness is preserved by this base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), so it is also of finite type by the definition of properness. Since an algebraically closed field is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes the geometric fibre a Noetherian scheme; it is therefore a proper Noetherian scheme. The assumed dimension bound applies to this fibre, and reduction has the same one-dimensional irreducible components appearing in the degree hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0D2S and 0B5Y, hypotheses on proper Noetherian fibres

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $x\to X$, with residue field extension $\kappa(x)\subset\overline{\kappa(x)}$. The degree hypothesis is exactly positivity on every one-dimensional irreducible component of the reduced geometric fibre, after normalization. Applying [lem-trf-fibre-degree-ample-criterion] to the proper Noetherian geometric fibre gives that $\mathcal L$ is ample there. The geometric fibre is of finite type over $\overline{\kappa(x)}$ by Step 1, so [lem-pc-very-ample-descends] applied to the faithfully flat field extension $\overline{\kappa(x)}/\kappa(x)$ descends this ampleness to the ordinary fibre $Y_{\kappa(x)}$. Thus the fibre ampleness required by [lem-trf-ample-neighbourhood] holds over the residue field. The zero-dimensional case is vacuous and gives the same conclusion.

Apply [lem-trf-ample-neighbourhood] at each point $x$ to the ordinary fibre ampleness established in Step 2. It gives an open neighbourhood $U_x$ on which $\mathcal L$ is relatively ample. Since $X$ is quasi-compact, choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$ refining these neighbourhoods. On each inverse image $Y_i=f^{-1}(U_i)$, the restricted line bundle is ample over the affine base $U_i$. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-ample-local] to these open immersions $U_i\to X$, viewed as an etale covering of the scheme $X$. The inverse images are schemes, and the neighbourhood theorem gives ampleness on every inverse image of an affine open in each $U_i$. Its last clause gives ampleness over every affine open of $X$. Thus $\mathcal L$ is $f$-ample; $f$ is quasi-compact because it is proper.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood; relative ampleness is local on the base: Morphisms Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), and the scheme specialization of Spaces Divisors Tag 0D36.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is finite type, $X$ is quasi-compact, and Step 3 has established $f$-ampleness. Apply [lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample] (Tag 01VU) to obtain $n\ge1$ such that $\mathcal N=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample over $X$. The evaluation clause of the same node (Tag 01VR) says that $\mathcal E=f_*\mathcal N$ is quasi-coherent, the evaluation map $f^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal N$ is surjective, and its associated canonical morphism $i:Y\to\mathbf P_X(\mathcal E)$ is an immersion with $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal N$. Finite type of $\mathcal E$ and closedness of $i$ are verified next.

The sheaf $\mathcal N=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is locally free of rank one. On a Noetherian affine trivializing open, the kernel of any map $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal N$ is the sheaf of the kernel of a matrix $A^r\to A$; this kernel is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Thus $\mathcal N$ is coherent locally, hence globally by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover] and the definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Proper coherent pushforward [lem-pc-coherent-hi], with $X$ locally Noetherian, makes $\mathcal E=f_*\mathcal N$ coherent, in particular finite type and quasi-coherent. The immersion $i$ of Step 4 has separated ambient morphism by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated]. Since $f$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $i$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes $i$ a closed immersion. Its pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ is $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, proving projectivity in the sense of [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02O5, Proposition proper-pushforward-coherent; Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample, clause (4), and Tag 01OD, projective-bundle separatedness; Algebra Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic) and Modules Definition 01BV (definition-coherent).

proof.text: Step 3 proves the asserted ampleness on every affine base open. Steps 4 and 5 supply the positive integer $n$, the finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$, and the required closed immersion with its specified pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$. These are exactly the asserted conclusions.
